Johnny, the youngest and most enthusiastic, bounced on the balls of his feet, practically vibrating with excitement. And finally, there was Violet, the troop's only female scout, sharpening her hatchet with practiced ease, her brow furrowed in concentration.
This weekend's camping trip was no ordinary outing. Troop 4 was on a quest – a quest for the legendary "Whispering Caverns," rumored to hold an ancient Native American artifact, the "Stone of Echoes." Dexter, who had spent countless hours poring over dusty maps and local folklore, claimed to have pinpointed its location.
"Alright, everybody," Hayden announced, clapping his hands. "Tomorrow, we follow Dexter's lead to the Whispering Caverns. Remember our motto: Be Prepared! Double-check your gear, get a good night's sleep, and let's make Troop 4 proud."
The next morning dawned bright and clear. Dexter, compass in hand, led the troop through dense undergrowth, the air thick with the scent of pine and damp earth. Aiden, as usual, was at the front, practically dragging Johnny along, while Violet kept a watchful eye on the rear, making sure no one fell behind.
The terrain grew increasingly challenging, forcing them to scramble over rocky outcrops and wade through icy streams. Joel's attempts at humor dwindled as the hike wore on, replaced by grunts of exertion. Matthew, initially meticulous, grew increasingly disheveled. Even Lucas, typically brimming with questions, fell silent.
Finally, after hours of relentless trekking, Dexter stopped abruptly, pointing towards a narrow crevice hidden behind a waterfall. "This is it," he whispered, his voice barely audible above the rushing water. "The entrance to the Whispering Caverns."
The entrance was barely wide enough to squeeze through. Hayden, ever cautious, insisted on exploring ahead with Dexter, leaving the others to wait. Time seemed to stretch on forever. Tension hung in the air, punctuated only by the roar of the waterfall.
Suddenly, a shout echoed from within the caverns. "Hayden! Dexter! Are you okay?"
They emerged, covered in dust and grime, their faces etched with a mixture of awe and apprehension. "It's… incredible," Hayden stammered. "But it's also… unsettling."
The caverns were a labyrinth of twisting tunnels and echoing chambers. Stalactites hung like frozen tears from the ceiling, while stalagmites rose from the floor like grotesque, otherworldly sculptures. As they ventured deeper, they noticed strange symbols etched into the walls, symbols that even Dexter couldn't decipher.
In the heart of the caverns, in a large, circular chamber, they found it: the Stone of Echoes. It was a smooth, grey stone, pulsing with a faint, ethereal light. As Johnny reached out to touch it, a low hum filled the chamber. Suddenly, the walls began to resonate with whispers – faint fragments of voices, murmuring in an unknown language.
The whispers intensified, growing louder and more insistent. Aiden, overwhelmed by the noise, clutched his ears and cried out. Violet, sensing the danger, grabbed Johnny's hand and pulled him away from the stone.
"We need to get out of here!" she shouted, her voice barely audible above the cacophony of whispers.
Panic set in as the whispers grew louder still, swirling around them, disorienting them. The scouts stumbled and floundered, their carefully planned formation dissolving into chaos.
It was Matthew, ever the organized one, who took the lead. Using his knowledge of knots, he tied a rope to a stalagmite and guided the others through the maze of tunnels, following the rope back towards the entrance.
They emerged from the caverns, blinking in the sunlight, their ears ringing, their nerves frayed. They didn't stop running until they were a safe distance away from the waterfall.
Later, huddled around the campfire, they recounted their experience, each adding their own details to the story. They decided to leave the Stone of Echoes undisturbed, understanding that some mysteries were best left unsolved.
That night, as they lay under the stars, Troop 4 learned a valuable lesson. The Whispering Caverns had tested their courage, their resilience, and their teamwork. They had faced their fears, relied on each other, and emerged stronger, more united than ever before. They hadn't brought back the Stone of Echoes, but they had brought back something far more valuable: a shared experience, a bond forged in the face of adversity, and a story they would tell for years to come. And as they drifted off to sleep, they knew that Troop 4 had truly earned their merit badges – not just in scouting skills, but in the art of friendship, courage, and the spirit of adventure.”
“The late afternoon sun dappled through the oak leaves as Troop 4 BSA gathered at their usual spot behind the community center. Aiden, the Senior Patrol Leader, unfurled a slightly crumpled map. "Alright, everyone, listen up! Camp Hemlock is just two weeks away, and we need to finalize our patrol assignments and gear checks."


A murmur went through the small group. The Phoenix Patrol, a lively bunch known for their diverse skills and occasional chaotic energy, huddled together. Lucas, their dependable Patrol Leader, tried to maintain a semblance of order.


"Phoenix Patrol, let's get organized," Lucas said, his voice calm amidst the low hum of excitement. "Hayden, you're in charge of our tech. Make sure all our devices are charged and any coding projects for camp are ready."


Hayden, his fingers already twitching as if hovering over a keyboard, nodded enthusiastically. "Got it, Lucas! I've even been working on a little program to help us identify constellations at night."


Joel, ever the gamer, chimed in, "Sweet! Maybe it'll be better than my usual method of just guessing based on what looks cool." He grinned, adjusting his slightly askew Troop 4 cap.


Matt, the patrol's resident trickster, couldn't resist. He subtly swapped Joel's cap with Nick's, who was busy inspecting his pocketknife. Joel, oblivious for a moment, reached up and frowned at the unfamiliar fit. Nick, equally confused, patted his own head. Laughter rippled through the patrol.


Lucas sighed good-naturedly. "Matt, focus! We need to make sure everyone has their gear in order. Johnny, how's your camping equipment looking?"


Johnny, a seasoned camper even at his young age, proudly displayed his neatly packed backpack. "Tent's waterproofed, sleeping bag's toasty, and I've got extra fire starters. Ready for anything!"


Aiden, observing the Phoenix Patrol's dynamic, chuckled. "Looks like you guys are almost there. Just make sure you coordinate on food and share the load. We don't want one person carrying all the weight."


The next few days were a flurry of activity. Hayden meticulously checked batteries and wrote lines of code. Joel, when not immersed in a virtual world, helped Lucas inventory their shared equipment. Matt, surprisingly helpful when focused, assisted Johnny in sharpening tent stakes. Nick, quiet but observant, made sure everyone had the necessary first-aid supplies.


The week before camp, Troop 4 held a practice overnight in a local park. The Phoenix Patrol, despite a few minor mishaps (Matt "accidentally" tied Joel's boots together while he slept, and Hayden's constellation app initially displayed more fictional planets than real ones), worked well together. Lucas's calm leadership kept them on track, and Johnny's camping expertise proved invaluable in setting up their campsite.


Finally, the day arrived for Camp Hemlock. The bus ride was filled with singing and anticipation. As they arrived at the sprawling campsite, the Phoenix Patrol eagerly unloaded their gear.


Their week at Camp Hemlock was a whirlwind of activities. They hiked through winding trails, learned about local wildlife, built impressive shelters, and even attempted (with varying degrees of success) to cook over an open fire. Hayden's constellation app, after a few debugging sessions, became a nightly hit. Joel discovered a new appreciation for the real world as he navigated the wilderness. Matt's pranks were mostly harmless and often broke the tension during challenging activities. Nick proved to be a steady and reliable member, always ready to lend a hand. And Johnny, as expected, thrived in the outdoor environment, sharing his knowledge and enthusiasm.


One evening, during a particularly intense game of capture the flag against the fierce Cobra Patrol, the Phoenix Patrol found themselves strategically outmaneuvered. Just as defeat seemed imminent, Lucas, thinking quickly, directed Hayden to use his knowledge of the terrain to create a diversion. Joel, surprisingly agile, used the chaos to flank the opposing team. Matt, with a well-timed (and slightly mischievous) deployment of a smoke bomb (approved by their Scoutmaster, of course), created enough confusion for Nick and Johnny to capture the flag.


Later, sitting around the crackling campfire, the Phoenix Patrol recounted their victory, laughter echoing through the trees. Aiden, observing them from a distance, smiled. The Phoenix Patrol, with their unique blend of skills and personalities, had proven that even a little bit of chaos could lead to great things, especially when guided by a capable leader like Lucas and fueled by the individual strengths of Hayden, Joel, Matt, Nick, and Johnny, with Johnny's camping prowess always a steadying force. They were Troop 4, and they were a team.”

Classic strawberry shortcake is perfect, full stop. A combination of tender golden shortcakes (a type of biscuit that first appeared in a 16th-century British cookbook), juicy strawberries, and a cloud of lightly sweetened cream, the recipe is as simple to make as it is delicious. It’s the ideal dessert for any holiday from the start of spring through at least the 4th of July, and it makes an excellent stand-in for birthday cake and other festive foods.
This strawberry shortcake recipe comes from Gourmet food editor emeritus Kemp Minifie in honor of her father’s favorite summer pastime: gathering fresh strawberries at a U-pick farm. Minifie offers a range of amounts of sugar you’ll use on the naturally sweet strawberries. After they’ve turned juicy, give them a taste; if you find you’ve used too much, a squeeze of lemon juice can even things out. (Outside of strawberry season, use the same method for blueberries, sliced peaches and plums, diced pears, or any juicy fruit that looks good to you.) Adding a dollop of sour cream to the whipped cream topping has a twofold effect: The result is more stable than plain whipped cream, and the slightly tangy topping makes a wonderful counterpoint to the sweet-tart berries.
Minifie uses barely sweetened buttermilk biscuits as the base here. You can make them up to a day in advance, or whip them together while the fruit macerates. Biscuits not your thing? Some variations use sponge cake instead, and the berries and cream would be equally delicious with pound cake or angel food cake.


Recipe information
   * Total Time
   * 1 hour 15 minutes (includes making biscuits)
   * Yield
   * 6 servings
Ingredients
Shortcakes:
1½ cups all-purpose flour
1½ Tbsp. granulated sugar
1½ tsp. baking powder
Rounded ¼ tsp. kosher salt
¼ tsp. baking soda
½ stick (2 oz.) cold unsalted butter, cut into ½" cubes
¾ cup well-shaken buttermilk
1 Tbsp. Milk or cream for brushing
Strawberries and Assembly:
2½ lb. strawberries, trimmed and quartered (7½ cups)
⅓ to ½ cup granulated sugar, or to taste
¼ tsp. kosher salt
1 cup chilled heavy cream
¼ cup sour cream
1½ to 2 Tbsp. powdered sugar
½ tsp. vanilla extract
Special Equipment
Potato masher
Preparation
   * Shortcakes:
Step 1
Put oven rack in the middle position and preheat oven to 425°F.
Step 2
Sift together flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and baking soda onto a sheet of wax paper, then sift again into a bowl. Blend butter into the dry ingredients with your fingertips until the mixture resembles coarse meal. Add buttermilk and stir with a fork until a dough just forms (dough will be moist).
Step 3
Turn the dough out onto a well-floured surface and knead gently 6 times. Pat out dough on a floured surface with floured hands, reflouring surface if necessary, into an 8x5½" rectangle. Trim all 4 sides with a knife, dusting knife edge with flour before each cut. Cut rectangle in half lengthwise, then into thirds crosswise to form 6 (2½") squares, flouring knife between cuts. Transfer shortcakes with a metal spatula to an ungreased baking sheet, arranging them 2" apart, and brush tops with milk or cream. Bake until pale golden, 12 to 15 minutes, then transfer to a rack to cool to room temperature.
   * Strawberries and Assembly:
Step 4
Toss strawberries with granulated sugar and salt in a large bowl and let stand 5 minutes. Gently press strawberries with a potato masher to help release their juices, being careful not to crush them to a pulp. Let stand at room temperature, stirring occasionally, 45 minutes to 1 hour.
Step 5
Beat together heavy cream, sour cream, powdered sugar (to taste), and vanilla in a medium bowl with an electric mixer at medium-high speed until very soft peaks form.
Step 6
Split shortcakes horizontally with a fork and arrange 2 halves, split sides up, on each of 6 plates. Top with strawberries and juices, then with whipped cream. 
   * Step 7 
   * Enjoy!

And then follow these instructions:

Round pans (8" or 9"): 20–25 minutes
9x13-inch pan: 35–40 minutes
Cool: Allow the cake to cool in the pan for 10 minutes before inverting it onto a wire rack to cool completely.

The Wolfie Style Rice: Master Guide (WARNING: Extremely Spicy)
Phase 1: Preparation (Pre-Cooking)
      * Objective: To prepare all ingredients and equipment before you start cooking.
      * Time: 10-15 minutes
      * Action:
      1. Chop the vegetables: Dice one medium onion into small, uniform pieces. Mince 4-6 cloves of garlic. Finely dice 3-4 Roma tomatoes and 1-5 Jalapeño (remove seeds for less heat, leave them in for more).
      2. Measure the rice: Measure out exactly 2 pounds of long-grain  rice.
      3. Measure the water: Measure out exactly 4.5 cups of water.
      4. Ready the sauce bottles: Have all 3 bottles of Peri-Peri sauce ready to go. One bottle for the rice pot, and two bottles for the separate sauce pot.
      5. Set up the pots: Have your main 5L pot for the rice and a separate smaller saucepan for the sauce on two different burners.
Phase 2: Cooking the Rice
      * Objective: To create a perfectly cooked, flavorful rice base.
      * Total Cooking Time: 32-35 minutes
      * Action:
      1. Heat the oil: Place your large pot on a burner over medium heat. Add 2 tablespoons of cooking oil or butter.
      2. Sauté the aromatics: Add the diced onion and jalapeño to the hot oil. Stir continuously for 3-5 minutes, or until the onion is soft and translucent. Now, add the minced garlic and diced tomatoes. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, until the tomatoes begin to break down slightly.
      3. Toast the rice: Add the 2 pounds of uncooked rice directly into the pot. Stir continuously for 2 minutes. This crucial step creates a barrier on each grain, ensuring a fluffy, non-sticky final texture.
      4. Add the liquids: Pour the entire 1 bottle of Peri-Peri sauce and the 4.5 cups of water into the pot. Add a pinch of salt. Stir just once to combine everything.
      5. Bring to a rapid boil: Increase the heat to high. Wait for the liquid to come to a full, rolling boil. This ensures the entire pot is at the correct temperature for even cooking.
      6. Simmer (15 minutes): As soon as a full boil is reached, immediately lower the heat to the lowest possible setting. Place the lid on the pot, ensuring it is tight-fitting. Set a timer for 15 minutes. DO NOT lift the lid or stir the rice during this time.
      7. Rest the rice (10 minutes): When the timer goes off, turn the heat off completely. Leave the pot on the burner with the lid on for an additional 10 minutes. The rice will finish cooking with the trapped steam. DO NOT lift the lid during this final, crucial step.
Phase 3: Cooking the Sauce
      * Objective: To create a rich, thick sauce to pour over the rice.
      * Time: 10-15 minutes (this runs concurrently with Phase 2)
      * Action:
      1. Pour the sauce: Pour the remaining 2 bottles of Peri-Peri sauce into a separate small saucepan.
      2. Simmer and reduce: Place the saucepan over low-medium heat. Let the sauce come to a gentle simmer. Cook for 10-15 minutes, or until it thickens to your preferred consistency. Stir occasionally to prevent it from sticking.

The fun is in the subtab, but I'm still going to write some Meetoball lore:
By a grill that was sizzling and hot,
Stood a man named Meetoball, a goofy old pot.
His apron was greasy, his spatula lost,
But he had a new method, no matter the cost.
He'd promised a feast, a burger galore,
But his spatula vanished, right out the back door.
"No matter!" cried Meetoball, with a twinkle in his eye,
"My toes are the tools, watch me make these things fly!"
With a wiggle and a jiggle, a squish and a stomp,
He patted the meat into a beefy, grey clump.
His small toes made dimples, a perfect little groove,
Ready for cheese, with a delicate move.
He tap-danced a rhythm right over the hot grill,
Flipping burgers with dexterity and unusual skill.
The neighbors all peeked, with a curious stare,
As Meetoball sang loudly, without a care.
"My feet are so clean!" he'd gleefully shout,
"I wash them with soap, there's no reason for doubt!"
He'd point at his arches, a proud, rosy pink,
"This flavor's unique, you just have to think!" 
The burgers were ready, some oval, some round,
From a man with ten toes, and peculiar sounds.
The family arrived, a hungry, loud crew,
And gazed at the patties, so strange and so new.
"Looks good, Cousin Meetoball," they cautiously said,
While wondering exactly how they were made.
They picked up their burgers, and took a small bite,
And found, to their shock, they were quite a delight!
He'd made them with love, and a dance for good measure,
A memory odd, and a questionable treasure.
And though it seemed strange, they all had to admit,
The hamburger toes were a hit.
Meetoball sat on a trampoline,
Chewing foot burgers—extra lean.
He flipped, he flopped, he spun in air,
Then crashed right through a folding chair.
He tried to juggle his ketchup jar,
But launched it clean into a car.
Then danced a jig with socks on fire,
While drinking juice from a car tire.
He built a throne from traffic cones,
Declared it “mine!” in twenty tones.
He surfed a fridge through outer space,
And slapped the moon right in the face.
Then stumbled down a mystic glade,
Where shiny swords in stones were laid.
He yanked one out with zero grace—
The ground exploded into bass.
Now Meetoball, with cosmic might,
Turned galaxies into disco light.
He ruled the stars from marshmallow thrones,
And made black holes on his mobile phones.
Planets bowed, dimensions swirled,
He was the ruler of every world.
All from foot burgers, greasy and grand—
The meal that conquered every land.
And though his crown was made of fries,
You’d still see ketchup in his eyes.
For Meetoball, both weird and true,
Was chaos king—forever chew.
ONLY ONE THING COULD DETHRONE MEETOBALL
AND ONLY ONE MAN.
SIMPLY BY REVEALING HIS TRUE NAME.

The people in the land of Malloria always lived in fear, for this was where he dwelled. He moved through the world like smoke. Armies fell before his shadow touched the ground. Mountains shattered beneath his gaze. Storms bowed as he passed. No one saw him arrive, no one saw him leave — only the aftermath of impossibility.
Then the sky tore open. A being stepped through the rift, claiming to rival him. The nameless one emerged from darkness, unshaken. Silence fell. The challenger struck — and was erased, for the power of the Legend was too powerful to withstand.
The rift widened. Countless forms spilled forth, each identical, each dangerous. Yet he did not move. He simply stood, a shadow stretching across the land, a shape that bent reality itself. 
Suddenly, the almighty being that protected the land’s voice boomed from out of the void: 
“The Living Legend has become too powerful. You must end his reign of terror!”
The Living Legend tilted his head, unseen and unknowable, a force older than fear itself.
“Finally,” he whispered, voice like the wind through shattered stone.
“I was growing bored.”
The world held its breath.
And the warrior of legend smiled.

We, the students, in order to foster a more engaging and collaborative learning environment, do hereby establish this Constitution. Recognizing the importance of both academic rigor and enjoyable learning experiences, we affirm our commitment to promoting inclusive educational practices that embrace the potential of games as a tool for growth, creativity, and camaraderie.


┊ **Article I: Purpose**  
Section 1. The purpose of this Constitution is to advocate for the incorporation of games as a means of enhancing our educational experience.  
Section 2. We acknowledge the valid concerns regarding the management of distractions and commit to using games responsibly and appropriately within the educational framework.




┊ **Article II: Rights of Students**  
Section 1. All students shall have the right to engage in educational activities, including the use of games, that facilitate learning and foster collaboration among peers.  
Section 2. Every student has the right to express their views regarding effective learning strategies, including the potential benefits of game-based learning.  


┊ **Article III: Responsibilities of Students**  
Section 1. All students are expected to maintain a respectful attitude towards their teachers and peers, utilizing games solely as educational tools.  
Section 2. Students shall be responsible for adhering to the guidelines established by school administration regarding gaming activities.  
Section 3. Each student must accept the rules and terms outlined in this Constitution, ensuring that their actions align with the broader goals of our educational community.


┊ **Article IV: Engagement with Faculty**  
Section 1. We encourage open communication between students and faculty regarding the integration of games into the curriculum.  
Section 2. Faculty are invited to consider feedback from students about the types of games that can be used to enhance learning while maintaining academic integrity.  


┊ **Article V: Unity and Support**  
Section 1. We shall unite as a student body to support one another in our educational pursuits, recognizing that collaboration is key to our success.  
Section 2. We pledge to help and encourage classmates who may be struggling, fostering an inclusive environment where everyone can thrive


┊ **Article VI: Amendments**  
Section 1. This Constitution may be amended by a two-thirds majority vote of the student body, should new ideas and strategies for improving our learning environment arise.


┊ **Conclusion**  
In signing this Constitution, we, the students. affirm our commitment to enhancing our educational experiences through collaboration, creativity, and the responsible use of games. We believe that together, we can create a vibrant learning environment that balances academic achievement with the joy of learning and friendship. Let us work in tandem with our teachers to build a school culture that values both diligence and play!

The building had 4 wooden pillars at the top of a stone stair case. the building itself was a massive stone biulding with a wooden roof. Kyle had never seen a building like this, it appeared to have 3 floors on the inside. "well go in the leaders inside" Tyler spoke holding the bird. Kyle stepped on the first step before heading up the stairs.


It took Kyle 20 secount to reach the top of the stairs case were he stood in-between 2 of the pillars. Kyle walked to the door before opening it , Unlike Oreji's sliding doors the door swung open. Inside sat a larges tables were chairs sat pushed in at the table it must be were they had there meeting. Inside there was 2 doors one each side, one must lead to were the leader was. Kyle looked left to right deciding witch door to go into. Kyle finally decided to go to the door on the right.


When Kyle passed the door he had entered a hall way with a lot more doors. who needed so many rooms? Kyle started to walk to the end of the hall were a door sat at the end. At the door at the end of the hall led to a stair case. Kyle put his foot on the wooden stair before climbing to the top. Kyle was now on the 3rd floor.


It took Kyle a few minutes to find the room Relano's leader was in. The leader was looking out as window when Kyle walked in. "hello there" the leader said turning his head to Kyle. "I have a warning, Warthif is planing on reopening the portal" Kyle said. "Tell me " the leader demanded.




Kyle sat down on the ground due to the fact there was nothing in the room, "well when Asuka from Sartuo  was attacked from Warthif, Carnis said some things about needed a bl00d sacrifice to open the portal" Kyle answered.  the leader now had a little worry in his eyes, "isn't it just a theory you need a bl00d sacrifice to open the portal?" the leader asked clearly trying to make it sound like it was just a rumor. "well this does sound like something Carnis would do, she probably doesn't know how to actually open the portal, she just trying the most popular rumor" Kyle said hoping to keep the leader from overthinking. "Well um  do you think the theory is fake?" the leader said. "well it seems real" he said.


" Thanks for the warning, I will look into it" The Relano leader said. "Kyle stood up "you might wanna prepare your village just in case". Kyle walked out of the room and closed the door. Did the leader believe Kyle, Kyle needed him to believe him.


Kyle walked to the end of the wooden staircase before heading to the bottom. he walked to the end of the hall entering the meeting room. the room was clearly untouched. Kyle had gone outside to find Tyler waiting outside. "so how'd  it go?" he asked.


"Well I don't know if he believed me, but he did say he would look into it" Kyle replied. "so  how long are ya planning on stayin" Tyler asked." to be honest I should start heading back now" Kyle said with a smile." It's a long walk to Oreji you should stay here for the night, ever used a cabin? Tyler said. " er-  well no ,Oreji just uses sheds.


"well there's a few open for use, but have you ever tried bird before?" Tyler said. "well we don't really catch them in Oreji, so I haven't" Kyle replied. "Well you got to try it, I'll cook it right now!"Tyler exclaimed. "follow me"Tyler said starting to walk, Kyle had nothing better to do so he followed. Tyler led him to the door of one of the cabins before he opened it, "this ones mine"he said signaling for Kyle to walk in.


Kyle entered the cabin, it was in fact a lot larger than the sheds Oreji had.  Kyle examined the wooden log  shaped walls in the cabin"dang a lot more room than mine!" Kyle exclaimed. Tyler shut the door behind him before walking over to the fire that was lit by a brick covered place. Tyler pulled out a d@gg3r  before   beheading the bird in his hand. Tyler laid down the head witch was now  dripping with bl00d.


Tyler's d@gg3r moved through the birds body as he cleaned out the bird organs. Tyler than put it onto a stake and put the birds body above the fire. "Well now we just wait" Tyler said.  "The bird's body that laid above the fire was clearly cooking as grease dripped from the bird. The smell of meet came from the flames.


After the bird had finished cooking Tyler had pulled the stake from the fire with the bird hanging on it smelling delicious."Sit down" Tyler said pointing to a table in the room with 5 chairs around it. Kyle walked over to the table before pulling a chair from the table and sitting in it.


Tyler put white discs on the table were Kyle sat and were Tyler pulled a chair for himself. "he then used a different d@gg3r to  cut the cooked bird in half placing one of the pieces on the disc object In Front of Kyle. Kyle took the half of the bird he had and bit into it. the flavor struck Kyles mouth as he bit into it, eh had never had bird before but this tasted pretty good.


"Taste pretty good!" Kyle exclaimed before taking another  bite of the bird. "Well im Glad ya like it" Tyler said smiling. Kyle took another bite of the bird, what should he say to Tyler without giving to much info about Oreji? he didn't want to reveal to much information. "so what's Oreji like? I've heard they have a nice river" Tyler asked. Speak of the portal Kyle thought, "well we mostly live in sheds, and the river is pretty nice" Kyle said.


Kyle finished his half of the bird he got. "well Its starting to get dark, I should head to Oreji" Kyle said standing up. "It's a long hike you should stay for the night and try a cabin, Ill lead you to a open one" Tyler replied standing up. Tyler walked to the door before opening it, Kyle walked through the door into the sunset sky. Tyler shut the door behind him before walking, Tyler lead him through the dark village of Relano.


Kyle followed closely behind Tyler hoping not to lose sight of him. Tyler suddenly turned around the corner of a cabin were he walked to the door of one. Kyle stoped by the door as well," well here we are" Tyler said as Kyle opened the door,Well see ya in the morning"he added as Kyle shut the door.  The stale air of the cabin came through Kyles nose, no one must have been in the cabin for a few years.  Kyle walked by a table that looked like the one he saw in Tylers room and over to the bed.


Kyle placed his Katanas next to the bed before laying down. the cabin was in fact a lot better than Oreji's  sheds the bed seemed more comfy than his own.Kyle looked around the room as it got darker as the sun vanished from the glass window by the bed. Kyle noticed a few strange shaped things on the walls. Kyle soon drifted into sleep.
